rationale_overall: Filtered a large amount of noise: ISS crew-rotation and astronaut-return stories (non-investable NASA/SpaceX ops, not a public-equity catalyst), war/missile reporting (Yemen-Israel, Gaza rocket fire, Pakistan military rocket-force commentary — geopolitical noise with no tradeable US ticker attached), private-company space news (SpaceX Starship/Falcon cadence, Blue Origin New Glenn — neither is public), local/education robotics human-interest pieces (Columbia youth robotics center, NYU Tandon, Temple College grant), foreign/OTC or agency nuclear items (China nuclear power framing, Vietnam-Korea MoIT talks, South Africa NECSA, India idrw), a Canadian junior uranium driller (OTC, sub-liquidity), and pure keyword false-matches (Rocket Arena concert venue, Rocket 105 radio, Starship Troopers video game, Fortnite's 'Rocket League'). The two candidate signals with real tickers were Rocket Lab's (RKLB) acquisition of Geost — a genuine buildup-phase catalyst in the rockets_spacecraft wave — and the Nvidia/AMD China export-tax story, which touches an already-held ticker (NVDA) rather than surfacing anything new. Given the weekly cadence and the requirement that any add be paired with a remove, neither rises to the bar of clearly displacing an intact AI mega-cap holding (AAPL/GOOGL/MSFT/NVDA all show no thesis breach this week); RKLB is noted as a watch item for a future rebalance once its buildup signal accumulates further evidence. Net effect: no change to the watchlist's thematic shape this week.
